rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A wing can mean either side; the human wings are the flanks, metaphorically named after a bird’s wings because it folds them in flight.
rows.anchor: قيل لكل ناحيتين : جناحان ، كجناحي العسكر لمجنبتيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means to place the hand against the side beneath the upper arm, as the following mention of its coming out shows.
rows.anchor: والمراد إلى جنبك تحت العضد ، دل على ذلك قوله : { تخرج }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-sūʾ means defect or ugliness generally and is a euphemism here for leprosy; Arabs loathed leprosy and its name, as in the euphemistic name al-Abraṣ for Jadīma, lord of al-Zabbāʾ.
rows.anchor: السوء : الرداءة والقبح في كل شيء ، فكني به عن البرص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed report says Moses was dark-complexioned and his hand emerged from his garment white, radiating like the sun and dazzling sight.
rows.anchor: يروي : أنه كان آدم فأخرج يده من مدرعته بيضاء لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both “white” and “sign” are circumstantial accusatives.
rows.anchor: { بيضاء } و { ءاية } حالان معا .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “without harm” attaches to “white,” as in saying something became white without harm.
rows.anchor: من غير سوء } من صلة لبيضاء ، كما تقول ابيضت من غير سوء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, “sign” is an object of an omitted verb such as “take” or “here you are,” recoverable from context.
rows.anchor: وفي نصب { ءاية } وجه آخر ، وهو أن يكون بإضمار نحو : خذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted command may connect to “that We may show you”: take this second sign after the staff becomes a serpent, so God may show some of His great signs through both signs; other construals make them the greatest signs or say the act was done to show them.
rows.anchor: أي خذ هذه الآية أيضا بعد قلب العصا حية لنريك بهاتين الآيتين بعض آياتنا الكبرى .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses recognized that facing Pharaoh the tyrant was a grave assignment requiring steadfastness and a broad, patient heart; he asked God to expand his chest and ease his task amid great affairs.
rows.anchor: عرف أنه كلف أمرا عظيما وخطبا جسيما يحتاج معه إلى احتمال ما لا يحتمله إلا ذو جأش رابط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The initial general requests are then specified as chest and task; this general-to-particular restatement makes the plea more emphatic than a direct request alone.
rows.anchor: قد أبهم الكلام أولا فقيل : اشرح لي ويسر لي ، فعلم أن ثم مشروحا وميسرا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Moses had a speech impediment, associated with the report of the ember.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس : كان في لسانه رتة لما روي من حديث الجمرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed report says Moses’s hand had been burned; Pharaoh tried to treat it without success, and Moses later pointed to the God who healed it despite Pharaoh’s inability.
rows.anchor: ويروي أن يده احترقت ، وأن فرعون اجتهد في علاجها فلم تبرأ ، ولما دعاه قال

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One reported explanation says the hand remained unhealed so Moses would not share a dish with Pharaoh and thereby incur the bond of eating together.
rows.anchor: وعن بعضهم : إنما لم تبرأ يده لئلا يدخلها مع فرعون في قصعة واحدة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view says the impediment partly remained, citing Moses’s brother as more eloquent and the claim that Moses scarcely spoke clearly.
rows.anchor: واختلف في زوال العقدة بكمالها فقيل : ذهب بعضها وبقي بعضها ، لقوله تعالى : { وأخى هرون

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says the impediment disappeared completely, citing God’s answer that Moses had been granted his request.
rows.anchor: وقيل : زالت بكمالها لقوله تعالى : { قد أوتيت سؤلك ياموسى * موسى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite “a knot,” rather than “the knot of my tongue,” indicates Moses requested only enough removal to be understood well, not perfect eloquence.
rows.anchor: وفي تنكير العقدة وإن لم يقل عقدة لساني : أنه طلب حل بعضها إرادة أن يفهم عنه فهما جيدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Of my tongue” is an adjective qualifying the knot, as though the phrase meant a knot among the knots of my tongue.
rows.anchor: و { من لساني } صفة للعقدة كأنه قيل : عقدة من عقد لساني .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wazīr may derive from burden: the minister bears the ruler’s burdens and expenses.
rows.anchor: الوزير من الوزر ، لأنه يتحمل عن الملك أوزاره ومؤنه .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, wazīr may derive from refuge: the ruler relies on the minister’s judgment and entrusts affairs to him.
rows.anchor: أو من الوزر ، لأن الملك يعتصم برأيه ويلجيء إليه أموره .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third derivation is from muʾāzara, meaning assistance.
rows.anchor: أو من المؤازرة وهي المعاونة .

rows.speaker: الأصمعي
rows.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī says the expected form would be azīr; the hamza shifted to wāw by analogy with related forms.
rows.anchor: عن الأصمعي قال : وكان القياس أزيرا ، فقلبت الهمزة إلى الواو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pattern faʿīl can carry the sense of mufāʿil; examples include ʿashīr, jalīs, qaʿīd, khalīl, ṣadīq, and nadīm.
rows.anchor: ووجه قلبها أن فعيلا جاء في معنى مفاعل مجيئا صالحا ، كقولهم : عشير وجليس وقعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One parsing makes wazīran and Hārūn the two objects of “make,” with Hārūn advanced for emphasis on the ministry.
rows.anchor: { وزيرا } و { هارون } مفعولا قوله { واجعل لي وزيرا من أهلي } قدم ثانيهما على أولهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, “for me a minister” supplies the two objects, and Hārūn is an explanatory apposition to minister; “my brother” is apposition to Hārūn.
rows.anchor: أو { لى وزيرا } مفعولاه ، وهارون عطف بيان للوزير . و { أخي } في الوجهين بدل من هارون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further parsing allows “my brother” to be another explanatory apposition; with the imperative reading it may instead be a nominative subject whose predicate is “strengthen my back by him.”
rows.anchor: على الابتداء : و { اشدد به } خبره ، ويوقف على { هارون }

rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: All readers have the two verbs as supplicatory imperatives, while Ibn ʿĀmir alone reads them as jussive responses.
rows.anchor: وابن عامر وحده ( اشدد ) و ( أشركه ) على الجواب

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd’s codex has “my brother” followed by “strengthen my back.”
rows.anchor: وفي مصحف ابن مسعود ( أخي واشدد )

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb’s codex places “make him share in my task” before “strengthen my back.”
rows.anchor: وعن أبي بن كعب ( أشركه في أمري واشدد به أزري )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-azr means strength; “strengthen my back” asks that Aaron reinforce Moses.
rows.anchor: الأزر : القوة . وأزره : قواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses asks for Aaron as a partner in the mission so they can cooperate in worship and remembrance; cooperation stirs effort and multiplies good.
rows.anchor: أي : اجعله شريكي في الرسالة حتى نتعاون على عبادتك وذكرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows their circumstances and that mutual support suits them; Aaron is an excellent support because he is older and more eloquent.
rows.anchor: وأن هارون نعم المعين والشاد لعضدي ، بأنه أكبر مني سنا وأفصح لسانا

none: Verse text only; the segment gives no commentary.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-wanā is slackness or shortcoming; one reading has the prefix vowel assimilated, yielding “do not slacken in remembering Me.”
rows.anchor: الونى . الفتور والتقصير . وقرىء ( تنيا ) بكسر حرف المضارعة للإتباع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means not to forget God; He remains in their remembrance wherever they go, and His remembrance is their source of aid and support, since affairs succeed through it.
rows.anchor: أي : لا تنسياني ولا أزال منكما على ذكر حيثما تقلبتما ، واتخذا ذكري جناحا تصيران به مستمدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Remembrance” may also mean conveying the message: dhikr covers worship generally, and conveying the message is among its greatest forms.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يريد بالذكر تبليغ الرسالة ، فإن الذكر يقع على سائر العبادات ، وتبليغ الرسالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report says God revealed to Aaron, while he was in Egypt, that he should meet Moses.
rows.anchor: روي : أن الله تعالى أوحى إلى هارون وهو بمصر أن يتلقى موسى .

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another account says Aaron heard that Moses was approaching.
rows.anchor: وقيل : سمع بمقبله .

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further account says Aaron was inspired to meet Moses.
rows.anchor: وقيل : ألهم ذلك .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading lightens layyinan to līnan, “gentle speech.”
rows.anchor: قرىء ( لينا ) بالتخفيف والقول اللين .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gentle invitation resembles the question and counsel, “Will you purify yourself? Shall I guide you to your Lord, so that you fear Him?”
rows.anchor: نحو قوله تعالى : { هل لك إلى أن تزكى * وأهديك إلى ربك فتخشى }

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view says they were to promise Pharaoh lasting youth, kingship until death, and continued pleasures of food, drink, and sex until he died.
rows.anchor: وقيل : عداه شبابا لا يهرم بعده ، وملكا لا ينزع منه إلا بالموت

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says they should avoid affronting Pharaoh and speak gently because he had raised Moses and had something like a father’s claim.
rows.anchor: وقيل : لا تجبهاه بما يكره ، وألطفا له في القول ، لما له من حق تربية موسى

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says they should address Pharaoh by a kunya; he had three: Abū al-ʿAbbās, Abū al-Walīd, and Abū Murra.
rows.anchor: وقيل : كنياه وهو من ذوي الكنى الثلاث : أبو العباس ، وأبو الوليد ، وأبو مرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hopeful wording instructs them to act expecting their effort may bear fruit, striving with all their strength rather than despairing.
rows.anchor: والترجي لهما ، أي : اذهبا على رجائكما وطمعكما ، وباشرا الأمر مباشرة من يرجو ويطمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sending messengers despite knowing Pharaoh would not believe establishes proof and removes his excuse, as the counterfactual at 20:134 shows.
rows.anchor: وجدوى إرسالهما إليه مع العلم بأنه لن يؤمن إلزام الحجة وقطع المعذرة { ولو أنا أهلكناهم بعذاب من قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To remember here is to reflect, consider, and then give oneself fairly to the truth.
rows.anchor: أي : يتذكر ويتأمل فيبذل النصفة من نفسه والإذعان للحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He may fear that Moses and Aaron’s warning is true and that denial will lead him to ruin.
rows.anchor: أن يكون الأمر كما تصفان ، فيجره إنكاره إلى الهلكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faraṭa means to precede or get ahead; al-fāriṭ reaches the watering place first, and a faras faraṭ is a horse that outruns others.
rows.anchor: فرط : سبق وتقدم . ومنه الفارط : الذي يتقدم الواردة . وفرس فرط : يسبق الخيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the basic reading, Moses and Aaron fear Pharaoh will hurry to punish them.
rows.anchor: أي : نخاف أن يعجل علينا بالعقوبة ويبادرنا بها .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading derives yufriṭ from a causative verb: they fear that some force will drive Pharaoh to act hastily.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( يفرط ) من أفرطه غيره إذا حمله على العجلة .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The force prompting haste could be Satan, Pharaoh’s arrogance and claim to divinity, his love of rule, or rebellious Coptic courtiers.
rows.anchor: خافا أن يحمله حامل على المعاجلة بالعقاب من شيطان ، أو من جبروته واستكباره وادعائه بالربوبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further reading takes the verb from excess in harm: they fear Pharaoh will abruptly block their delivery of the message.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( يفرط ) من الإفراط في الأذية ، أي : نخاف أن يحول بيننا وبين تبليغ الرسالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Pharaoh might exceed bounds in punishing them, given his known viciousness and arrogance.
rows.anchor: أو يجاوز الحد في معاقبتنا إن لم يعاجل ، بناء على ما عرفا وجربا من شرارته وعتوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unqualified, allusive “or transgress” politely avoids openly voicing the enormity Pharaoh might commit against God.
rows.anchor: بالتخطي إلى أن يقول فيك ما لا ينبغي ، لجرأته عليك وقسوة قلبه .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “With you” means God protects and supports them; hearing and seeing what happens between them and Pharaoh, He will do what protection and support require.
rows.anchor: {معكما } أي حافظكما وناصركما { أسمع وأرى } ما يجري بينكما وبينه من قول وفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hearing and seeing may take their words and actions as explicit objects, or the verbs may stand without an expressed object, meaning that God is their watchful protector.
rows.anchor: فجائز أن يقدر أقوالكم وأفعالكم ، وجائز أن لا يقدر شيء ، وكأنه قيل : أنا حافظ لكما وناصر سامع مبصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since their protector and helper hears and sees, protection is secure and they need not fear the enemy.
rows.anchor: وإذا كان الحافظ والناصر كذلك ، تم الحفظ وصحت النصرة ، وذهبت المبالاة بالعدو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh and the Copts held the Israelites in bondage, imposing digging, construction, carrying stones, and other forced labor, while killing their sons and enslaving their women.
rows.anchor: كانت بنو إسرائيل في ملكة فرعون والقبط ، يعذبونهم بتكليف الأعمال الصعبة : من الحفر والبناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement about bringing a sign explains the claim to be the Lord’s messengers, since the claimed mission requires its proof.
rows.anchor: جملة جارية من الجملة الأولى وهي { إنا رسولا ربك } مجرى البيان والتفسير ، لأن دعوى الرسالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular “a sign” is generic proof of their claim even though they brought two miracles.
rows.anchor: ولم يثن ومعه آيتان : لأن المراد في هذا الموضع تثبيت الدعوى ببرهانها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The greeting is the angels, guardians of Paradise, welcoming those who follow guidance, while Hell’s guardians rebuke the deniers.
rows.anchor: يريد : وسلام الملائكة الذين هم خزنة الجنة على المهتدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation from earth refers to the creation of humanity’s origin, Adam, from it.
rows.anchor: أراد بخلقهم من الأرض خلق أصلهم هو آدم عليه السلام منها .

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another account says an angel takes soil from the place where a person will be buried and scatters it over the sperm, so the person is created from both soil and sperm.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إن الملك لينطلق فيأخذ من تربة المكان الذي يدفن فيه فيبددها على النطفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Returning people to earth means their scattered parts mixed with soil are reassembled and restored alive, then brought to the gathering place.
rows.anchor: وأراد بإخراجهم منها أنه يؤلف أجزاءهم المتفرقة المختلطة بالتراب ، ويردهم كما كانوا أحياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He connects the resurrection to the swift emergence from graves described at 70:43.
rows.anchor: يوم يخرجون من الأجداث سراعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God lists the earth’s benefits: a bed and cradle, paths, plants for human food and animal fodder, humanity’s origin and mother, and finally its role as a shroud.
rows.anchor: حيث جعلها لهم فراشا ومهادا يتقبلون عليها ، وسوى لهم فيها مسالك يترددون فيها

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet is quoted as saying, “Make contact with the earth, for it is kind to you”; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: ومن ثم قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( 686 ) ( تمسحوا بالأرض فإنها بكم برة )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening expression may be an accusative governed by an omitted verb, or a predicate of an omitted subject; it means “choose either of the two” or “the choice is yours to cast or ours.”
rows.anchor: { أن } مع ما بعده إما منصوب بفعل مضمر . أو مرفوع بأنه خبر مبتدإ محذوف . معناه : اختر أحد الأمرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sorcerers show good manners, humility, and deference, offering Moses a fair choice; God may have inspired their courtesy.
rows.anchor: وهذا التخيير منهم استعمال أدب حسن معه ، وتواضع له وخفض جناح ، وتنبيه على إعطائهم النصفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses chose that they throw first, both answering their courtesy and allowing them to display their magic before God’s miracle defeats it.
rows.anchor: وعلم موسى صلوات الله عليه اختيار إلقائهم أولا ، مع ما فيه من مقابلة أدب بأدب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here idhā is a temporal adverb used for sudden occurrence, governed by an omitted verb of surprise; the clause depicts Moses suddenly confronted by ropes and staffs seeming to move.
rows.anchor: والتحقيق فيها أنها إذا الكائنة بمعنى الوقت ، الطالبة ناصبا لها وجملة تضاف إليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading has ʿuṣiyyihim with ḍamma, the original form; the kasra comes by vowel assimilation.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( عصيهم ) بالضم وهو الأصل بالكسر إتباع ونحوه : دلي ودلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading attaches the verb to the ropes and staffs, with “that they were moving” as an inclusive apposition, like “Zayd pleased me, his generosity.”
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( تخيل ) على إسناده إلى ضمير الحبال والعصي وإبدال قوله : { أنها تسعى } من الضمير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading makes the ropes and staffs seem to display movement; a reflexive reading means that they appeared to imagine it.
rows.anchor: وتخيل . بمعنى تتخيل . وطريقه طريق تخيل .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further reading has God as the one making the illusion for the trial and test.
rows.anchor: ونخيل : على أن الله تعالى هو المخيل للمحنة والابتلاء .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the sorcerers smeared their ropes and staffs with mercury; sunlight made them quiver, creating the illusion of motion.
rows.anchor: يروى : أنهم لطخوها بالزئبق ، فلما ضربت عليها الشمس اضطربت واهتزت .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite wording generalizes the trick: what they made was sorcery, in worldly or otherworldly activity of that kind.
rows.anchor: المراد تنكير الأمر ، كأنه قيل : إن ما صنعوا كيد سحري . وفي سعي دنيوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means wherever the sorcerer comes or acts, like “wherever he was sent,” “whichever way he went,” and “wherever.”
rows.anchor: { حيث أتى } كقولهم : حيث سير ، وأية سلك ، وأينما كان

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: A saying attributed to ʿUmar illustrates the general indefinite use: “not in a worldly matter nor in another matter.”
rows.anchor: وفي حديث عمر رضي الله عنه : لا في أمر دنيا ولا في أمر آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unattributed poetic line, “in worldly striving that has long been extended,” supplies an example of worldly usage.
rows.anchor: في سعي دنيا طالما قد مدت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentary marvels at the reversal: the sorcerers threw their ropes and staffs in disbelief, then soon threw themselves down in gratitude and prostration.
rows.anchor: سبحان الله ما أعجب أمرهم . قد ألقوا حبالهم وعصيهم للكفر والجحود ثم ألقوا رؤسهم بعد ساعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report says the converts did not raise their heads until they saw Paradise and Hell and the reward of their inhabitants.
rows.anchor: وروي : أنهم لم يرفعوا رؤوسهم حتى رأو الجنة والنار ورأوا ثواب أهلها

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima says that while they prostrated God showed them the places in Paradise to which they would go.
rows.anchor: وعن عكرمة : لما خروا سجدا أراهم الله في سجودهم منازلهم التي يصيرون إليها في الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation of “your chief” is that Moses was their greatest sorcerer, highest in skill and rank.
rows.anchor: لعظيمكم ، يريد : أنه أسحرهم وأعلاهم درجة في صناعتهم .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, kabīr means teacher: Meccans called a teacher or instructor “my elder.”
rows.anchor: أو لمعلمكم ، من قول أهل مكة للمعلم : أمرني كبيري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading lightens the forms of both the threats to cut off and crucify.
rows.anchor: قرىء ( فلأقطعن ) ( ولأصلبن ) بالتخفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cutting “crosswise” means cutting the right hand and left foot, opposite limbs.
rows.anchor: والقطع من خلاف : أن تقطع اليد اليمنى والرجل اليسرى ؛ لأن كل واحد من العضوين خالف الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min marks the starting point of cutting, which arises from opposing rather than matching limbs; the phrase is circumstantial, describing them as cut in differing ways.
rows.anchor: و ( من ) لابتداء الغاية ؛ لأن القطع مبتدأ وناشيء من مخالفة العضو العضو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrasing “in the palm trunks” likens the crucified person’s firm placement to an object lodged in its container.
rows.anchor: شبه تمكن المصلوب في الجذع بتمكن الشيء الموعى في وعائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Which of us” refers to Pharaoh and Moses, as shown by Pharaoh’s claim that the converts believed Moses before Pharaoh gave permission.
rows.anchor: { أينا } يريد نفسه لعنه الله وموسى صلوات الله عليه بدليل قوله : { له قبل }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Qurʾānic usage the lām with īmān can refer to belief in someone other than God, as at 9:61.
rows.anchor: واللام مع الإيمان في كتاب الله لغير الله تعالى ، كقوله تعالى : { يؤمن بالله ويؤمن للمؤمنين } ( التوبة : 61 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh boasts of his power and familiar tortures, belittles and mocks Moses, and threatens him although Moses had never tortured anyone.
rows.anchor: وفيه نفاجة باقتداره وقهره ، وما ألفه وضري به : من تعذيب الناس بأنواع العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses asks what prevented Aaron from following him in defending God and forcefully restraining disbelief and sin; why he did not fight the unbelievers, act as Moses would have, or catch up with him.
rows.anchor: والمعنى ما منعك أن تتبعني في الغضب لله وشدة الزجر عن الكفر والمعاصي ؟ وهلا قاتلت من كفر بمن آمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To stretch one’s eyes is to prolong one’s gaze without turning away, admiring and desiring to possess what is seen.
rows.anchor: مد النظر : تطويله ، وأن لا يكاد يرده ، استحسانا للمنظور إليه وإعجابا به ، وتمنيا أن يكون له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning recalls onlookers who wished for Qarun’s wealth at 28:79 and were answered by people of knowledge and faith at 28:80.
rows.anchor: كما فعل نظارة قارون حين قالوا : { الدنيا ياليت لنا مثل ما أوتى قارون إنه لذو حظ عظيم } ( القصص : 79 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An incidental glance followed by lowering the eyes is excused; the verse rebukes sustained looking, a habit encouraged by worldly adornment.
rows.anchor: وفيه أن النظر غير الممدود معفو عنه ، وذلك مثل نظر من باده الشيء بالنظر ثم غض الطرف

rows.speaker: العلماء من أهل التقوى
rows.claim: Pious scholars insist that believers must avert their gaze from the buildings, clothing, mounts, and other display of oppressors and profligates, since looking fulfills their desire for an audience and encourages them.
rows.anchor: ولقد شدد العلماء من أهل التقوى في وجوب غض البصر عن أبنية الظلمة وعدد الفسقة في اللباس والمراكب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Azwājan means groups or kinds of disbelievers.
rows.anchor: { أزواجا منهم } أصنافا من الكفرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the phrase is circumstantial from the pronoun, with the verb applying to “them”: people among those whom God has given enjoyment.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن ينتصب حالا من هاء الضمير ، والفعل واقع على { منهم } كأنه قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One analysis puts zahrah in the accusative as a term of censure or specification.
rows.anchor: على الذم وهو النصب على الاختصاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second analysis treats muttiʿnā as carrying the sense “gave and bestowed,” making zahrah its second object.
rows.anchor: وعلى تضمين { متعنا } معنى أعطينا وخولنا ، وكونه مفعولا ثانيا له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third analysis makes zahrah a substitute for the case position of the prepositional phrase.
rows.anchor: وعلى إبداله من محل الجار والمجرور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth analysis makes zahrah a substitute for azwājan, with an implied “possessors of.”
rows.anchor: وعلى إبداله من أزواجا ، على تقدير ذوي زهرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With its vowel moved, zahrah retains its sense of adornment and beauty; the author compares jahrah and cites the reading “Show us God” at 4:153.
rows.anchor: معنى الزهرة بعينه وهو الزينة والبهجة ، كما جاء في الجهرة الجهرة . وقرىء : { أرنا الله } ( النساء : 153 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it may be a plural of zāhir, describing worldly people as radiant in complexion and appearance from their indulgence, unlike the pallor and coarse clothing of the righteous.
rows.anchor: وأن تكون جمع زاهر ، وصفا لهم بأنهم زاهرو هذه الدنيا ، لصفاء ألوانهم مما يلهون ويتنعمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their worldly enjoyment may be a test that makes them deserve punishment because they are ungrateful, or it may mean God will punish them in the afterlife for it.
rows.anchor: لنبلوهم حتى يستوجبوا العذاب ، لوجود الكفران منهم . أو لنعذبهم في الآخرة بسببه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Lord’s provision may mean the stored reward of the afterlife, better in itself and more lasting.
rows.anchor: هو ما ادخر له من ثواب الآخرة الذي هو خير منه في نفسه وأدوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it means the blessing of Islam and prophethood that God grants.
rows.anchor: أو ما رزقه من نعمة الإسلام والنبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may mean lawful provision: the disbelievers’ wealth is often stolen or illicit, and God ascribes only what is lawful and pure to Himself; forbidden wealth is not called provision.
rows.anchor: والحرام لا يسمى رزقا أصلا

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abū Rāfiʿ reports that the Prophet sent him to request a loan from a Jewish man until Rajab; the man demanded collateral, so the Prophet pledged his iron armor and said he was trustworthy in heaven and earth. The source says this verse was revealed in connection with the incident; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: بعثني رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى يهودي وقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām may simply complement iqtaraba.
rows.anchor: هذه اللام : لا تخلو من أن تكون صلة لاقترب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the lām emphasizes that the reckoning is ascribed to the people; this parsing is more unusual than treating it as a complement.
rows.anchor: أو تأكيدا لإضافة الحساب إليهم ، كقولك : ( أزف للحي رحيلهم ) الأصل أزف رحيل الحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The near event is the Hour; when it approaches, its reckoning, reward, punishment, and other events also approach.
rows.anchor: والمراد اقتراب الساعة ، وإذا اقتربت الساعة فقد اقترب ما يكون فيها من الحساب والثواب والعقاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrasing parallels “the true promise has drawn near” at 21:97.
rows.anchor: ونحوه : { واقترب الوعد الحق } ( الأنبياء : 97 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although more than five hundred years had passed, the Hour is near in God’s reckoning, as 22:47 says one day with God is like a thousand years by human counting.
rows.anchor: والدليل عليه قوله عز وجل : { ويستعجلونك بالعذاب ولن يخلف الله وعده وإن يوما عند ربك كألف سنة مما تعدون } ( الحج : 47 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anything still awaited is near, however long its expected arrival; what is truly distant is what has already occurred and ended.
rows.anchor: ولأن كل آت وإن طالت أوقات استقباله وترقبه قريب ، إنما البعيد هو الذي وجد وانقرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The remaining life of the world is shorter than what has passed, as shown by the advent of the final Prophet, whose mission was foretold for the end time.
rows.anchor: ولأن ما بقي في الدنيا أقصر وأقل مما سلف منها ، بدليل انبعاث خاتم النبيين الموعود مبعثه في آخر الزمان

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet is quoted as saying, “I was sent in the breath of the Hour”; no grading is given.
rows.anchor: وقال عليه السلام : ( 691 ) ( بعثت في نسم الساعة )

rows.speaker: بعض المتقدمين
rows.claim: A sermon by one of the early predecessors says the world has turned its back and only a small remainder remains, like a little liquid in a vessel.
rows.anchor: وفي خطبة بعض المتقدمين : ولت الدنيا حذاء ، ولم تبق إلا صبابة كصبابة الإناء .

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says “the people” refers to the polytheists, using the generic name for a subset because the following description identifies them.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : أن المراد بالناس : المشركون . وهذا من إطلاق اسم الجنس على بعضه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are heedless of their account and final fate despite reason requiring recompense for good and evil; when warned, they turn away and shut their ears.
rows.anchor: وصفهم بالغفلة مع الإعراض ، على معنى : أنهم غافلون عن حسابهم ساهون ، لا يتفكرون في عاقبتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both yūḥā (passive) and nūḥī (active, “We reveal”) are established readings.
rows.anchor: {يوحى } ونوحي : مشهورتان .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse restates and confirms the preceding verses on divine oneness.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية مقررة لما سبقها من آي التوحيد .

rows.speaker: خزاعة
rows.claim: The passage was revealed about Khuzāʿa, who claimed that the angels were daughters of God.
rows.anchor: نزلت في خزاعة حيث قالوا : الملائكة بنات الله .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is transcendent above begetting; the angels are His servants, and servitude is incompatible with parentage. Their honored rank near Him, due to their special qualities, misled people into calling them His children.
rows.anchor: نزه ذاته عن ذلك ، ثم أخبر عنهم بأنهم عباد والعبودية تنافي الولادة ، إلا أنهم { مكرمون } مقربون عندي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has mukramūn.
rows.anchor: وقريء ( مكرمون )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading vocalizes lā yasbiqūnahu with ḍamma, deriving it from sābaqtuhu fa-sabaqtuhu.
rows.anchor: و { لا يسبقونه } بالضم ، من : سابقته فسبقته أسبقه .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels follow God’s speech and say nothing until He says it; their actions likewise follow His command, and they do nothing without being commanded.
rows.anchor: والمعنى : أنهم يتبعون قوله ولا يقولون شيئا حتى يقوله ، فلا يسبق قولهم قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in “by the speech” stands in for possessive annexation: they do not precede His saying with their saying.
rows.anchor: والمراد : بقولهم ، فأنيب اللام مناب الإضافة ، أي لا يتقدمون قوله بقولهم

words: يعلم ما بين أيديهم وما خلفهم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All their deeds, past and future, are in God’s sight and He will repay them; knowing this, they restrain themselves, guard their conduct, and fill their time with worship.
rows.anchor: وجميع ما يأتون ويذرون مما قدموا وأخروا بعين الله ، وهو مجازيهم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their vigilance includes interceding only for those God approves and qualifies for greater reward and honor.
rows.anchor: ومن تحفظهم أنهم لا يجسرون أن يشفعوا إلا لمن ارتضاه الله وأهله للشفاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are apprehensive of God, alert even to a slight sign, continually cautious and never secure from His plan.
rows.anchor: أي متوقعون من أمارة ضعيفة ، كائنون على حذر ورقبة لا يأمنون مكر الله

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet is reported to have seen Gabriel on the Night Journey collapsed like a worn saddlecloth from fear of God; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: وعن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( 695 ) أنه رأى جبريل عليه السلام ليلة المعراج ساقطا كالحلس

words: ومن يقل منهم إني إله من دونه
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The severe warning against an angel claiming divinity applies hypothetically, though God knows it will never happen; like 6:88, it magnifies shirk and the importance of pure monotheism.
rows.anchor: فاجأ بالوعيد الشديد ، وأنذر بعذاب جهنم من أشرك منهم إن كان ذلك على سبيل الفرض والتمثيل ، مع إحاطة علمه بأنه لا يكون
